correctness.rationale: The chord-exposure reduction uses strict convexity of K_p and regular C^1 radial parametrization. At each axis gamma(alpha+t)=(1-|t|^p/p+o(|t|^p),t+o(t)), so the normal error of an adjacent chord tends to J_p(u,s)/p after dividing by h^p. The tail away from axis tips is <= C N^{p-2} h^p, vanishing in the double limit p<2. Symmetric decreasing rearrangement of the Green interpolation kernel bounds J_p<=2^{-p}, with equality at u=-1/2,s=1/2; for integer u the maximum is (p-1)p^{-p/(p-1)} at u=0,s=p^{-1/(p-1)}. Divisibility by 4 controls axis-grid alignment. Independent chord-gap optimization at p=1.25,1.5,1.75 with n=256..259 reproduces ratios 0.9479..0.9997 and local grid evaluation verifies the universal interpolation bound; p=1.25,n=512,1024 improve the integer-grid ratios to 0.96393,0.97481. Finite checks do not prove n->infinity. Domain fixed 1<p<2, Euclidean Hausdorff, unit radial grid.

value.rationale: The arithmetic phase resonance is a natural sharp rate for a specified polygon approximation of a singular-curvature convex body. Distinct constants for grids hitting or straddling four axis tips quantify a genuine discretization boundary beyond smooth curvature asymptotics. This is a meaningful exact invariant of a natural sampling rule, not an arbitrary n residue slice invented after computation.
